cards.scope: score of 10.00 for a single routine
cards.claim: Perfect 10 refers to a score of 10.00 for a single routine in artistic gymnastics.
cards.quote: Perfect 10 (gymnastics) Perfect 10 refers to a score of 10.00 for a single routine in artistic gymnastics, which was once thought to be unattainable—particularly at the Olympic Games—under the code of points set by the International Gymnastics Federation (FIG).

cards.claim: Perfect 10 refers to a score of 10.00 for a single dive in diving.
cards.quote: Perfect 10 (diving) Perfect 10 refers to a score of 10.00 for a single dive in diving, which was once thought to be unattainable—particularly at the Olympic Games—under the rules set by the International Swimming Federation (FINA).

cards.scope: Sport associated with a Perfect Score
cards.claim: A perfect score of 300 is associated with the sport of bowling, as evidenced by references to the United States Bowling Congress Hall of Fame and the Weber Cup, which is a team challenge event in bowling.
cards.quote: of 300 games have been broadcast on live TV. Grazio Castellano of Brooklyn, New York was the first to roll a on live television. This occurred on October 4, 1953, during an Eastern All-Star league session at Newark, New Jersey. (Castellano is a member of the United States Bowling Congress Hall of Fame.) A more recent example of this came in October 2006, when England's Paul Moor became the first man to register a score of 300 in the Weber Cup (the first 300 on live British television), the annual Europe versus America team challenge event.
